excerpt: The desktop app runs an MCP server, so ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex and Cursor can search your footage and edit your projects from their own chat.
Cloud agents like Dot, Muse, Grok Bot and Devin install Kino on their own computer and edit while you’re away.
Ask for the cut. The agent reads your footage, makes the edit, and leaves every clip on the timeline for you to move.
Built upon Remotion and optimized for fast playback, you can also tweak any detail within Kino’s “what you see is what you get” editor.
Manage many variants of your video and ask the agent to one-shot each.
Start with craft. 100+ templates: titles, maps, captions and transitions. Bring them in or ask your agent to take inspiration from them.
Every clip is transcribed, described shot by shot, and knows who’s in it.
Terabytes scrub locally, and every clip is transcribed, described, and searchable.
Save a filter and it becomes a smart bin that fills as footage arrives.
RED, Blackmagic RAW, ProRes, DNxHR and MXF play as the camera or Avid wrote them.
Every clip streams from Kino, so a project opens the same on any machine.
Send a link. Comments land on your timeline, and the agent can answer them.
No account needed.
Share any clip as a link, and search by what’s on screen.
Edit together, share review links and get notes back.
Paste a render for review, share every asset as one package, or hand a node to your agent.

Ran Kino head-to-head with Claude Code directly to make a simple video. Kino was much easier to nudge and control, and the user praised it as something that "just works", which they say is rare in software.
"actually really enjoying kino.ai, a bit more user friendly than hyperframes but I find claude to be a bit worse?? it's very usable though so maybe just a weird prompt on my end"

A user understood Kino to be most effective when you already have footage, not when starting from scratch. They mostly use Claude to make small explainer videos for themselves or teammates and felt Kino wasn't the right fit for that.

A user who made recurring podcasts noted that templates were missing. They wanted to reuse the same format, title design, intro music, trailer clips and social cuts so an agent could produce a full episode from a few commands. They called an agent-guided template builder "the holy grail."
